mainTopic: The seven-day פרישה of the כהן גדול and the פרה כהן, the name לשכת פרהדרין, and the start of a discussion about bakers and דמאי.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about two כהנים who are separated for seven days. The כהן גדול before יום כפור is separated for קדושה, so other כהנים may touch him. The כהן who burns the פרה אדומה is separated for טהרה, so they may not. The גמרא says this ברייתא follows רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי, not רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, because by his view there would also be a difference about הזאה. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא then challenges the practice of sprinkling all seven days, because sprinkling on the fourth day can never help. The גמרא answers that 'seven days' already skips שבת, so it can skip the fourth day too. רבא adds that the פרה כהן is separated on Wednesday, so that his fourth day falls on שבת. The גמרא then explains why the room was called לשכת פרהדרין: the כהנים גדולים who bought the position were replaced every year. Finally it quotes a משנה from מסכת דמאי about bakers and begins to ask about it. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: why one sequestered כהן may be touched and the other may not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by explaining that the כהן גדול is separated for holiness, while the פרה אדומה כהן is separated for purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this one (the כהן גדול) is separated for holiness, so his fellow כהנים may touch him. But that one (the פרה אדומה כהן) is separated for purity, so his fellow כהנים may not touch him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that gives a difference between the כהן גדול before יום כיפור and the כהן who burns the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two separations have different goals. The כהן גדול is separated to prepare him with awe and holiness, so being touched is no problem. The פרה כהן is separated to keep him extra טהור, so others may not touch him and risk passing on טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Separation / sequestering of a כהן before his special service
Holiness; here, spiritual preparation
Ritual purity
His fellow כהנים
Touch

steps.confusionAlert: Both כהנים are separated for seven days. The difference is the PURPOSE of the separation, and that purpose decides whether touching is allowed.

phrases.english: For this one, his separation is for holiness
phrases.notes: Refers to the כהן גדול before יום כיפור.

phrases.english: and his brother priests may touch him,
and this one, his separation is for purity
phrases.notes: Refers to the כהן who burns the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: and his brother priests may not touch him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול's separation is for קדושה, so he may be touched. The פרה כהן's separation is for טהרה, so he may not.

steps.title: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא matches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion this ברייתא fits. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only ONE difference between the two כהנים, the touching. The גמרא wants to know which opinion allows for there being just one difference.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Which opinion does this follow?)

phrases.english: According to whom?
phrases.notes: Just one word in the גמרא, and it's a question the גמרא asks all the time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the only difference between the two sequestered כהנים is touching.

steps.title: It follows רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי, not רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים
steps.stepSummary: Only by רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי is touching the sole difference. By רבי חנינא there is also a difference in הזאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows either רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי. For if it followed רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, there would be this other difference too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי. It cannot follow רבי חנינא, because by him there is a second difference the ברייתא would have mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, three views were taught. רבי מאיר says both כהנים get הזאה all seven days. רבי יוסי says both get it only on the 3rd and 7th days. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים splits them: the פרה כהן all seven days, the כהן גדול only on the 3rd and 7th. Since the ברייתא mentions no הזאה difference, it must be one of the first two views.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי חנינא, the deputy כהן גדול
Deputy (second-in-command to the כהן גדול)
But there is also this (another difference)!

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'הָא אִיכָּא נָמֵי הָא' does not spell out the extra difference. You must recall from earlier that it is about הזאה: all seven days versus only the 3rd and 7th.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: Either Rabbi Meir or Rabbi Yosei.
For if it were Rabbi Chanina the deputy High Priest,
there is also this (other difference).
phrases.notes: The other difference is sprinkling all seven days versus only the 3rd and 7th.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי, because by רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים there would be a second difference (הזאה) that the ברייתא would have listed.
steps.whatToRemember: A list that gives only ONE difference tells us the author holds there is no other difference. Here that rules out רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.

steps.title: Setup of the challenge: most days can be justified as a possible 3rd or 7th day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא shows that sprinkling on days 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 makes sense, because each could be the 3rd or 7th day of his טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא objected. It makes sense for the first day: maybe it is his third day of טומאה. The second: maybe it is his third. The third: maybe it is his third. The fifth: maybe it is his seventh. The sixth: maybe it is his seventh. The seventh: maybe it is his seventh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא begins an attack on sprinkling all seven days. First he lists the days that DO make sense, setting up his real question about day four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is טמא מת needs sprinkling of פרה אדומה ashes on the 3rd and 7th days of his טומאה. We worry the כהן may have become טמא just before his separation without knowing. Each day of the separation could then line up with his 3rd or 7th day of טומאה, which justifies sprinkling on it.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it strongly
It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this works, but…' challenge)
Perhaps
Third (day of טומאה)
Seventh (day of טומאה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'רִאשׁוֹן', 'שֵׁנִי' and so on count days of the SEPARATION (פרישה). 'שְׁלִישִׁי' and 'שְׁבִיעִי' after 'שֶׁמָּא' count days of the טומאה. These are two different counts.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina objected:
Granted the first day: perhaps it is the third.
phrases.notes: He may have become טמא two days before the separation.

phrases.english: The second: perhaps it is the third.
The third: perhaps it is the third.
The fifth: perhaps it is the seventh.
The sixth: perhaps it is the seventh.
The seventh: perhaps it is the seventh.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the author of the ברייתא to challenging the seven-day הזאה practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the פרה כהן receives הזאה all seven days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it shows which days are justified, preparing to show that one day is not.

steps.title: The real challenge: sprinkling on the fourth day accomplishes nothing
steps.stepSummary: Day four of the separation cannot be his 3rd day of טומאה, and if it were his 7th, sprinkling would not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on the fourth day, why do I need sprinkling at all? There is no doubt that it is his third day, and there is no doubt about it being a useful seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the punch of the challenge. On the fourth day of separation, sprinkling serves no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It cannot be his 3rd day of טומאה, since he has been guarded from טומאה for three full days. If it were his 7th day, he became טמא three days before the separation, so his 3rd day fell before the separation with no sprinkling. Without a 3rd-day sprinkling, a 7th-day sprinkling is useless.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of water mixed with פרה אדומה ashes
Why do I need it?
To be in doubt about

steps.whyThisMatters: The challenge forces us to see that 'seven days of הזאה' may not be literal. The next steps resolve this.

phrases.english: But the fourth day,
why do I need sprinkling at all?
There is no doubt about it being the third,
phrases.notes: He has been guarded for three days already.

phrases.english: nor is there a doubt about it being the seventh?
phrases.notes: A 7th day without a 3rd-day sprinkling would not help.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רְבִיעִי לְמָה לִי הַזָּאָה כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא… אלא' structure begun in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sprinkling all seven days, specifically on the fourth day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Day four can be neither a possible 3rd day nor a useful 7th day of טומאה, so sprinkling on it has no purpose.

steps.title: Counter-question: even 'all seven days' was never literal because of שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that הזאה cannot happen on שבת, so 'seven days' already had an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, is there ever really sprinkling on all seven days? Don't we hold that הזאה is a rabbinic שבות and does not override שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its defense by turning the question around. It shows that the 'seven days' could never have meant every single day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים forbade הזאה on שבת as a שבות, and it does not push aside שבת. Any seven-day separation must include a שבת. So 'seven days' already means seven days with a gap, and this opens the door for the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning…
We have an established rule
A rabbinic prohibition made to protect the rest of שבת
Overrides / pushes aside

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
is there sprinkling all seven days?
But we hold
that sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition (on שבת)
and it does not override שבת!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, הַזָּאָה כׇּל שִׁבְעָה מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with a counter-question that undermines its literal reading of 'seven days'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The challenger's assumption that 'all seven days' means literally every day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of שבת, the seven days always included a day without הזאה, so 'seven' cannot be fully literal.

steps.title: Resolution: seven days except the fourth, just like seven days except שבת
steps.stepSummary: Just as 'seven days' excludes שבת, it also excludes the fourth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? Seven days except שבת. Here too: seven days except the fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. 'Seven days of הזאה' means seven days minus the fourth day, just as it means seven days minus שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we accept that שבת is an exception, adding a second exception is easy. The fourth day is skipped because sprinkling then does nothing, which resolves רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's challenge. 'Seven days' describes the whole period, not every single day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say?
Except for / apart from
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of הזאה 'all seven days' for the פרה כהן really means every day of the seven except two: שבת, when הזאה is forbidden as a שבות, and the fourth day, when sprinkling has no possible use.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
Seven days except for שבת,
here too,
seven days except for the fourth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the שבת comparison in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of a term by analogy ('seven days' is not literal, like the שבת exception).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Seven days' meant sprinkling on literally every day, so day four is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Seven days' means seven days minus the fourth, just as it already means minus שבת.

steps.title: רבא: the calendar decides for the כהן גדול, but we choose the day for the כהן of the פרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that the כהן גדול must be separated on ג׳ תשרי no matter which weekday it is. The כהן השורף את הפרה is separated on Wednesday, so his fourth day falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Therefore, the כהן גדול on יום כפור, where it does not depend on us but on when the month was fixed, must be separated on ג׳ תשרי, and whenever ג׳ תשרי falls, we separate him. But the כהן who burns the פרה, where it does depend on us, we separate on Wednesday, so that his fourth day falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the rule we just learned (no הזאה on שבת or on the fourth day) and shows how it plays out in practice for the two כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום כפור is fixed on י׳ תשרי, so the separation must begin on ג׳ תשרי, whatever weekday that is. As a result, the fourth day and שבת can be two different days without הזאה. For the פרה there is no fixed date, so we begin on Wednesday and make the two 'no sprinkling' days the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore (a practical conclusion)
The fixing of the new month (by בית דין)
The month of ראש השנה and יום כפור
The כהן who burns the פרה אדומה
The fourth day of the week (Wednesday)

steps.whatToRemember: כהן גדול: the calendar decides, so we begin on ג׳ תשרי. פרה: we decide, so we begin on Wednesday and his fourth day falls on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'fourth days' here. 'רביעי בשבת' means Wednesday, the fourth day of the week. 'רביעי שלו' means the fourth day of his own seven-day separation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא caring about the practical schedule. Where we have a choice, we arrange things so that as few days as possible go without הזאה.

phrases.english: Rava said: Therefore
the High Priest on Yom Kippur
where the matter does not depend on us
rather the matter depends on the fixing of the month
phrases.notes: The date of יום כפור depends on when ראש חודש תשרי was set.

phrases.english: he must be separated on the third of Tishrei
and whenever the third of Tishrei happens to fall
we separate him.
But the priest who burns the heifer
where the matter depends on us
we separate him on the fourth day of the week (Wednesday)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּנִיתְרְמֵי רְבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: so that his fourth day will fall on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: That way, the day with no sprinkling (הזאה) and שבת end up being the same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 7 (both שבת and the fourth day are excluded) to real scheduling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כהן גדול is separated on ג׳ תשרי whatever the weekday. The כהן השורף את הפרה is separated on Wednesday so that his fourth day coincides with שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה questions the name of the chamber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next words of the משנה, 'ללשכת פרהדרין', and quotes רבי יהודה asking why it is called that, when it was really called לשכת בלווטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To the לשכת פרהדרין.' It was taught: רבי יהודה said: Was it really called the לשכת פרהדרין? Wasn't it called the לשכת בלווטי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new phrase in the משנה. A ברייתא challenges the name the משנה used for the כהן גדול's chamber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרהדרין are short-term officials, replaced every year, so the name sounds lowly. בלווטי means distinguished ministers, which seems more fitting for the כהן גדול's room. רבי יהודה asks which name is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Chamber of the פרהדרין (officials appointed for one year)
Chamber of the ministers or council heads
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: To the Chamber of Parhedrin.
It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says
And was it the Chamber of Parhedrin?
Wasn't it the Chamber of Balvatei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: explaining a term in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The name 'לשכת פרהדרין' used in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The chamber was known as לשכת בלווטי, so why does the משנה call it by a different name?

steps.title: Why the name changed from Balvatei to Parhedrin
steps.stepSummary: At first it was called לשכת בלווטי. Later, people bought the כהונה גדולה with money, and the כהנים גדולים were replaced every year like the פרהדרין, so the chamber was renamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, at first they called it the לשכת בלווטי. But because people paid money for the כהונה, and the כהנים גדולים were replaced every twelve months like these פרהדרין, who are replaced every twelve months, they began calling it the לשכת פרהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains that both names are correct, each from a different period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original, honorable name was בלווטי. Once unworthy people bought the position, they did not last the year and were replaced annually. The new name, פרהדרין, compares them to yearly officials and is meant as criticism.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, originally
Money
The priesthood (here, the position of כהן גדול)
They replace
Twelve months

steps.whatToRemember: Both names are correct. בלווטי was the original honorable name, and פרהדרין came later because the כהנים גדולים changed every year.
steps.whyThisMatters: The name itself is a criticism of the corrupt period of the Second Temple, when the כהונה גדולה was bought.

phrases.english: Rather, at first they would call
it the Chamber of Balvatei.
But because they give money for it, for the priesthood

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחֲלִיפִין אוֹתָהּ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: and they replace it every twelve months
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול was replaced every year.

phrases.english: like these parhedrin

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמַּחְלִיפִין אוֹתָם כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: who are replaced every twelve months
therefore they would call it
the Chamber of Parhedrin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בַּתְּחִלָּה הָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ לִשְׁכַּת בָּלְווֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's question about the name.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical: each name belongs to a different period
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one name can be correct.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name changed from בלווטי to פרהדרין when the כהנים גדולים began being replaced every year.

steps.title: A משנה about bakers and doubtfully tithed produce
steps.stepSummary: Connected to the לשכת פרהדרין, the גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת דמאי: the חכמים required bakers to separate only תרומת מעשר and חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: The חכמים obligated bakers to separate only תרומת מעשר and חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source from another מסכת. It is setting up the next step, which asks about this משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bakers buy grain from many people, some of whom may not have tithed it. This grain is called דמאי. The חכמים made it easier for bakers by requiring only two gifts, תרומת מעשר and חלה, and left out the other gifts. The next steps ask why the other gifts are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Bakers
One tenth of מעשר ראשון, given to a כהן
A portion of dough given to a כהן
Produce whose tithing is in doubt

phrases.english: We learned there (in a Mishnah):
Bakers
the Sages did not obligate them to separate
except terumat maaser and challah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prompted by the mention of פרהדרין; opens a related הלכה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bakers buying דמאי must separate only תרומת מעשר and חלה.

steps.title: Conceding that תרומה גדולה is not needed, and introducing a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that bakers do not need to separate תרומה גדולה from דמאי, and introduces a ברייתא that explains why.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that תרומה גדולה is not required, as a ברייתא teaches:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question about the משנה in מסכת דמאי. It first agrees that one gift, תרומה גדולה, clearly does not need to be separated, and it is about to quote a ברייתא that explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'I understand this part.' The גמרא is not challenging the rule about תרומה גדולה. It is agreeing with it first so that it can then ask about a different gift, which the משנה also leaves out and which is harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted' / 'It makes sense': the opening of a question that first agrees with one part before asking about another part
The main תרומה, the first portion of produce given to a כהן
'As it was taught': introduces a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, where we are unsure if it was tithed

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא is not the question itself. It is only the 'I understand' half. The real difficulty comes in the next line, which will begin with 'but' (אלא).

phrases.english: Granted, teruma gedola is not required,
phrases.notes: The גמרא accepts this part of the משנה's ruling without difficulty.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה in מסכת דמאי does not require bakers to separate the other gifts. The answer for תרומה גדולה is conceded first, and the real question comes next.
